description: This file defines an abstract base class for Keycloak's client registration test suite. It sets up a dedicated test realm populated with users holding different administrative permission levels, such as managing clients, creating clients, or no access at all. It provides reusable helper methods for creating and retrieving clients through the Client Registration service, as well as for authenticating as each of the predefined test users. Concrete test classes extend this class to verify authorization rules around dynamic client registration without duplicating realm and user setup logic.

This file implements a Freemarker template model bean used to render the list of applications a user has interacted with in the account management console. It gathers all non-bearer-only clients the user has consent records or role access for, then computes which realm and client roles the user can potentially receive. It also tracks granted client scopes, offline token grants, and filters out clients the user cannot access unless consent could change that. Nested classes represent individual application entries and client role details for display purposes.

This file provides a Freemarker model bean supporting the User-Managed Access (UMA) resource sharing pages in Keycloak's account console. It exposes a user's owned resources, resources shared with them, and pending permission requests awaiting approval from either side. Nested classes model resources, resource servers, permission requesters, granted scopes, and associated policies, translating internal authorization store entities into view-friendly representations. It enforces that a user can only access resources they own when a specific resource is requested via the URL.

This file implements the 'get-roles' subcommand of the Keycloak admin command-line interface (kcadm). It defines command-line options for targeting a specific user, group, client, or composite role, and for filtering results as available, effective, or including all client roles. The class validates that mutually exclusive option combinations are not used together, resolves human-readable identifiers to internal IDs via REST calls, and builds the appropriate Admin REST API URL before delegating execution to the parent GetCmd class. It also defines detailed usage and help text for the command.

This file implements a container class for holding cryptographic keys and content encryption key (CEK) material used during JSON Web Encryption (JWE) operations. It stores separate encryption and decryption keys, along with a serialized and decoded representation of the CEK keyed by usage type (encryption or signature). It lazily generates or deserializes the CEK bytes through a pluggable JWEEncryptionProvider when needed. This class centralizes key state so JWE encryption and decryption logic can share it consistently.

This file models a generic LDAP directory entry within Keycloak's LDAP integration layer. It stores the entry's distinguished name, unique identifier, object classes, and attributes, keeping a case-insensitive lookup map alongside the original attribute names. It also tracks read-only attribute names and manages paginated (ranged) attribute values that LDAP servers sometimes return in chunks. Equality and hashing are based on the entry's UUID, and a descriptive toString method aids debugging and logging of LDAP object state.

This file implements the factory responsible for creating and configuring the OpenID Connect (OIDC) login protocol within Keycloak. It defines the built-in protocol mappers for standard claims like username, email, name, address, and phone number, and registers them under default client scopes such as profile, email, address, and phone. It also sets up specialized scopes for roles, web origins, and Microprofile JWT claims, and applies default client settings such as redirect URIs and web origins when new clients are created. This factory is central to how Keycloak issues ID tokens and access tokens conforming to the OIDC specification.

This file contains UI test cases for the personal information page of Keycloak's account console. It verifies that a user can update their username, email, first name, and last name, and that changes persist and display correctly after navigation. It also tests form validation behavior, including rejecting empty required fields and detecting duplicate usernames or emails against another test user. An additional test confirms that disabling the edit-username setting correctly locks that field while still allowing other profile updates to be saved.

This file defines a WildFly/JBoss management resource for configuring Keycloak's theme subsystem within an application server. It declares configurable attributes such as static resource cache max age, whether themes and templates are cached, the welcome theme, the default theme, the themes directory path, and additional theme modules. These attributes are registered as read-write management attributes that trigger a service restart when changed. The class also provides a lookup method to retrieve an attribute definition by its XML name, supporting the subsystem's management model.

This file implements Keycloak's central manager for storing, validating, and updating user credentials such as passwords and OTPs. It routes credential operations to either local storage or federated storage depending on whether the user originates from an external user storage provider, and delegates validation and updates to registered credential providers or storage-specific handlers. It supports checking whether a credential type is configured for a user, disabling credential types, and authenticating users through storage providers that support direct authentication. It also participates in user cache invalidation and propagates cache population events to credential providers.

This file implements an adapter that exposes a Keycloak user's profile fields, such as username, email, first name, last name, and custom attributes, through the common UpdateProfileContext interface. It wraps a UserModel and RealmModel so that profile update flows can read and modify a real user's data without depending on the concrete user implementation. It also checks the realm setting that controls whether username editing is permitted. This context is used during required actions like the update profile flow triggered after login.
